task: Write one sentence of your own using the word convoluted. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know convoluted should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Explaining the league's convoluted playoff format took the commissioner eleven slides and a decision tree.
An involved procedure has many steps but stops short of convoluted — the steps still run in one followable line.
Labyrinthine goes further than convoluted: not just twisted but a full maze, built as if to lose you.

Tangled is the everyday word for things twisted together into knots — headphone cords, schedules, testimony. Convoluted is the sharper, more formal criticism: it says something was made with too many turns, so that following one thread drags you through every twist of the rest.

Circuitous describes a single path that wanders instead of going straight — the long way around, in a drive or an explanation. Convoluted is knottier: nothing about it runs in one line; its parts twist back through one another until the thread is hard to hold.

Convoluted means intricate and complicated.
The estate's convoluted will sent the lawyers in circles: the house passed to a trust, the trust answered to a foundation, and the foundation's only trustee was the tenant of the house.
Convoluted is more pointed than 'complicated' — from Latin volvere, 'to roll,' it describes something so coiled in on itself that following one thread drags you through every twist of the rest.
Convoluted criticizes structure: plots, procedures, and explanations with too many turns.
Its unit-mate abstruse excuses the material (it runs deep); convoluted blames the maker — this could have been straight, and isn't.
